content: Antiretroviral (ARV)-related toxicities are among the most frequently reported reasons for non-adherence to antiretroviral therapy (ART), as well as for discontinuation or substitution of medications. Understanding the prevalence of these toxicities is essential for informing national guidelines and implementing strategies to prevent and mitigate drug-related toxicities. The number of ART patients who discontinue or switch treatment due to toxicity during a reporting period is compared to the total number of ART patients in the same period. This data is typically collected from program records, such as ART registers, cohort reporting forms, and patient records. Treatment-limiting toxicity is defined as a serious adverse drug reaction that necessitates discontinuation or substitution of the drug. Data can be disaggregated by gender (male, female, transgender), age (<15, 15+), key populations (e.g., men who have sex with men, people in prisons, people who inject drugs, sex workers, transgender individuals), and pregnant or breastfeeding women. The percentage of people living with HIV on ART who initiate tuberculosis (TB) preventive treatment (TPT) is a critical indicator of efforts to prevent TB-related morbidity and mortality. Recent guidelines have expanded eligibility criteria for TPT among people living with HIV. The numerator includes ART patients who initiated TPT, while the denominator includes all eligible ART patients. Data is collected from program records, and disaggregation includes gender, age (<5, 5–15, 15+), type of TPT regimen, and ART initiation status (new on ART in the last 12 months or on ART for more than 12 months). Many countries have made progress in initiating TPT, but completion rates remain low or unknown. This indicator assesses the proportion of patients who complete the recommended course of TPT. The numerator includes ART patients who completed TPT, while the denominator includes those who initiated TPT in the previous reporting period. Data is collected from program records, and disaggregation includes gender, age (<15, 15+), type of TPT regimen, and ART initiation status. The percentage of people living with HIV who are newly initiated on ART and have active TB disease is an indicator of the burden of TB among this population. Early detection of TB enables prompt treatment and early ART initiation. The numerator includes people living with HIV newly initiated on ART who have active TB, while the denominator includes all newly initiated ART patients. Data is collected from program records, and disaggregation includes gender, age (<15, 15+), and key populations. Viral suppression at delivery is assessed among women on ART who deliver in a facility and have a viral load test. The numerator includes HIV-positive pregnant women on ART who are virally suppressed (viral load <1000 copies/mL) at delivery, while the denominator includes those on ART who deliver in a facility and have a viral load test. Data is collected from program records, and disaggregation includes age (<15, 15–19, 20–24, 25+) and timing of ART initiation (during pregnancy or already on ART at the first antenatal care visit). Early testing supports timely ART initiation for those with confirmed HIV infection and counseling for those with negative results. The numerator includes HIV-exposed infants who received a virological test within two months of birth, while the denominator estimates the number of HIV-positive women who delivered during the reporting period. Data is collected from program records, and disaggregation includes test results (HIV-positive, HIV-negative, indeterminate) and infant age (<2 months, 2–12 months). The numerator includes HIV-exposed infants started on ARV prophylaxis at birth, while the denominator includes HIV-positive women who delivered within the past 12 months. Data is collected from program records, and disaggregation includes age and timing of ART initiation. The numerator includes HIV-positive pregnant women who delivered and received ART, while the denominator includes all HIV-positive pregnant women who delivered during the reporting period. Data is collected from program records, and disaggregation includes age and timing of ART initiation. The numerator includes breastfeeding infants whose mothers are on ART, while the denominator includes HIV-exposed infants attending maternal and child health services for a 12-month visit. Data is collected from program records, and disaggregation includes age and timing of ART initiation. The numerator includes HIV-exposed infants with known final outcome status, while the denominator includes HIV-positive women who delivered within the past 12 months. Data is collected from cohort birth tracking, and disaggregation includes outcome status (HIV-positive, HIV-negative, no longer breastfeeding). The numerator includes women tested for syphilis, while the denominator includes all women attending antenatal care services. Data is collected from program records, and disaggregation includes age and timing of testing. The numerator includes seropositive women who received treatment, while the denominator includes all seropositive antenatal care attendees. Data is collected from program records, and disaggregation includes age. The numerator includes women who report ever having a screening test, while the denominator includes all survey respondents. Data is collected from representative surveys, and disaggregation includes age and test results. The numerator includes survey respondents who report avoiding healthcare due to stigma, while the denominator includes all survey respondents. Data is collected from representative surveys, and disaggregation includes age and key population type. The numerator includes those who report receiving a defined package of prevention services, while the denominator includes all surveyed key population members. Data is collected from surveys, and disaggregation includes age and key population type.
